subject.title: Feature: Add per-model generation timeout config

question: Should OpenClaw add a typed per-model generation/request timeout under `agents.defaults.models`, or should operators use provider/run timeout surfaces while semantic loop safeguards stay tracked separately?
rationale: The change adds a public config/default surface in a timeout area that already has several adjacent controls, so automation should not choose the permanent contract name, precedence, and migration expectations without maintainer intent.

options.title: Define a per-model timeout contract
options.body: Add a typed field with documented precedence and runtime enforcement for selected fallback candidates, then align docs/schema/tests around that single contract.

options.title: Keep provider/run timeout surfaces only
options.body: Close or narrow this request and direct operators to `models.providers.<id>.timeoutSeconds` or provider-level `request.timeoutMs` once that separate work lands.

options.title: Split semantic loop handling
options.body: Keep this issue focused on time budgets and leave repeated-content or thinking-loop detection to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/44965 and related bug reports.

recommendation.title: Define a per-model timeout contract
recommendation.body: Add a typed field with documented precedence and runtime enforcement for selected fallback candidates, then align docs/schema/tests around that single contract.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the clearest maintainer-facing review of the exact remaining config and runner boundary.
